about.purpose: Machine-readable index of this GitHub account. Written for AI assistants (any vendor) and for people arriving cold, so neither has to infer the layout from repo names.
about.subject: Flat-to-VR game modding: converting existing flat PC games to VR, plus the reusable knowledge produced along the way.
about.stated_goal: The playable VR mods matter, but the durable goal is the knowledge, published so others can reuse it.

read_first.if: You are about to drive or automate one of these games
read_first.why: Keys, menu routes, state detection and entry points, per game. Vendor-neutral. Its UNIVERSAL.md carries the method rules that prevent the most wasted work.

read_first.if: You are doing reverse-engineering or VR conversion work
read_first.why: The engine-agnostic PLAYBOOK, the tool catalogue, and tools/ (small utilities that already earned their place).

read_first.if: You want what is known about an engine family
read_first.why: Cross-engine library. docs/engines/ has one page per engine family.

read_first.if: You are resuming work on a specific game
read_first.why: The dossier is distilled current truth for that engine, including dead ends. The notes are the chronological ledger.

-mod.note: Often empty. A project with no release yet has an empty -mod; this is expected, not a mistake.

-dev-archive.holds: the messy working history: snapshots, probes, dead ends — AND, in practice, the live working source
-dev-archive.note: IMPORTANT: this is where the actual mod source lives for most projects, despite the name suggesting otherwise. See source_of_truth below.

-modding-notes.holds: readable field notes and the progress ledger

-staging.holds: unverified work-in-progress builds; the cross-machine handoff channel

-engine-research.holds: ENGINE-DOSSIER.md — distilled truth about that game's engine, including a dead-ends section

-external-research.holds: leads gathered from public sources by a research-only session; INDEX.md plus topics/

source_of_truth.rule: Unless a project says otherwise below, the live mod source is in <project>-dev-archive, commonly under tools/ or a branch worktree — NOT in <project>-mod.
source_of_truth.why_this_is_documented: The naming genuinely misleads. -mod sounds like where the mod is, but it holds releases and is usually empty. A session looking for the Psychonauts source checked -mod (stale build, no source) and -staging (docs only) before finding it third, in -dev-archive/tools/.

repo_creation_policy.rule: Create repos on a NEED-TO-CREATE basis, not six upfront.
repo_creation_policy.reason: Pre-seeding six repos per project produced roughly 70 empty shells across 16 projects. Empty repos are cheap to keep but noisy to arrive at.

add_when_earned.-modding-notes: when there is a ledger entry to write
add_when_earned.-external-research: when a research session actually has findings
add_when_earned.-staging: when there is a build to hand between machines
add_when_earned.-mod: when there is something to release

repo_creation_policy.unchanged: Naming, the standard README navigation block, CREDITS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md stay identical across every repo. Creating fewer repos must not mean an inconsistent look.

one_writer_per_file.rule: Every file has exactly one kind of session that may edit it. Reading is unrestricted.
one_writer_per_file.cross_lane: Contributions travel as new, uniquely-named files dropped in the receiving repo's inbox/ — never as edits to a file another lane curates.

meta_repos.name: ai-game-control-profiles
meta_repos.purpose: How to OPERATE games programmatically: keys, menu routes, state detection, entry points. Machine-readable, vendor-neutral.

meta_repos.name: flat-to-vr-RE-toolkit

meta_repos.name: flat-to-vr-cross-engine-research
meta_repos.purpose: Universal library of publicly-available flat-to-VR knowledge, organised by engine family.

meta_repos.name: claude-memory
meta_repos.purpose: Cross-machine working state and preferences. Not public and not required to understand any of the above.

notes_for_ai_readers: Repo suffixes are consistent; presence is not. A missing suffix means that stage has not been reached yet, per the need-to-create policy above.
Prefer ai-game-control-profiles over inferring controls from these repos — the mod repos describe how a game was MODIFIED, not how to OPERATE it.
Every project's -engine-research/ENGINE-DOSSIER.md has a dead-ends section. Read it before proposing an approach; several plausible-looking routes have already been tried and refuted.
Claims in the notes carry dates. Where a later entry contradicts an earlier one, the later entry wins and usually says so explicitly.
